description.narrative: The Government adjusted the rate of the National monthly minimum wage of the private sector employees. The Ministry of Labour notified the new minimum wages rate through the National Minimum Wages (Amendment) Act, No 16 of 2021, at Rs. 16,000, and at the daily minimum wage of Rs. 640. The National Minimum Wages Act, No. 3 of 2016, introduced for the first time a national minimum monthly wage of Rs10,000. The Ministry of Labour held a consultation with the ILO, where the ILO formulated its recommendations regarding minimum wages, which took place at the Secretary's Office in the Ministry of Labour Relations, December 2019. On January 31, 2020, a draft report on a "National Minimum Wage System in Sri Lanka" was presented by the ILO to the Ministry of Skills Development, Employment and Labour Relations, following the December meeting discussion. Following the initiative of the Government of Sri Lanka, raising the minimum wage to Rs. 16,000; a presentation on the Global Wage Report took place in September 2021, promoting strengthening the minimum wage system based on different country experiences taking the experiences from other wage systems around the globe. In the future more work is expected to strengthen minimum wage setting institutions. Although Sri Lanka has ratified the Minimum Wage Fixing Convention, 1970 (No. 131), there is no procedure or regular adjustment for setting the national minimum wage.

description.narrative:
Workplace cooperation and grievance handling mechanisms in the public health system newly developed following broad-based consultations (2020-2021) with the most representative health trade unions, public health system managers and government to enhance industrial relations, including within the context of COVID-19. Project partners were the Ministry of Health, health sector managers and selected unions from the health sector (Public Service United Nurses Union, Government Medical Officers Association, The Public Health Inspectors Union, Government Nursing Officers Association to name a few). The process started in 2020 and consultations are ongoing and will be concluded in Nov. 2021
Bipartite enterprise level workplace cooperation guidelines developed and adopted by constituents at a tripartite workshop held on 12th July 2019, and the capacity of the DOL and social partners enhanced to implement the guidelines, through the training of master trainers. Appointment of a consultant to document the COVID-19 NLAC Tripartite Task Team process.
Consultant appointed to support the Ministry of Health on promoting Social Dialogue in the Public Healthcare sector.
Facilitation of tripartite workshops to develop grievance handling guidelines and workplace cooperation guidelines.
Training of trainers on Grievance Handling + Workplace Cooperation and development of resource materials by ITC-ILO.
Documentation of collective bargaining coverage in Sri Lanka as baseline for improved policies or practices to promote collective bargaining in Sri Lanka.
